# GoldAlert — Full Reference

## What this tool does
GoldAlert is a free, browser-based dashboard for monitoring gold, silver, gold
mining stocks, gold/silver ETFs, and gold-backed cryptocurrency in real time,
and for applying a simple, transparent tiered signal to any of them.

## The signal rule (exact mechanics)
A trading day is marked "red" when its closing price is lower than the
previous trading day's closing price. Based on the current consecutive
red-day streak for an asset:
- 0–2 consecutive red days: HOLD
- 3–4 consecutive red days: 50% BUY / WATCH
- 5 or more consecutive red days: 100% BUY / STRONG
An optional minimum total percentage decline can also be required before a
streak counts. This is a rule-based, backtestable observation — it is not a
prediction, and it is not financial advice.

## Assets tracked and their exchange symbols
- Gold — spot gold, USD per troy ounce
- Silver — spot silver, USD per troy ounce
- AngloGold Ashanti — NYSE:AU (gold mining stock)
- Kinross Gold — NYSE:KGC (gold mining stock)
- Harmony Gold — NYSE:HMY (gold mining stock)
- Gold Fields — NYSE:GFI (gold mining stock)
- VanEck Gold Miners ETF — AMEX:GDX (mining-sector ETF)
- SPDR Gold Shares — AMEX:GLD (physically-backed gold ETF)
- iShares Silver Trust — AMEX:SLV (physically-backed silver ETF)
- Pax Gold — PAXG (gold-backed cryptocurrency, one token ≈ one troy ounce)
- Tether Gold — XAUT (gold-backed cryptocurrency, one token ≈ one troy ounce)

Note: Kinesis Gold (KAU) was evaluated and deliberately excluded — it trades
across only a handful of small exchanges with fragmented, inconsistent
pricing, unlike the two gold-backed tokens above which have deep, verifiable
liquidity.

## Features
- Real-time TradingView charts (ticker tape, advanced chart with symbol
  switching, and category-tabbed market-overview widgets).
- A signal board showing every tracked asset at once: latest close, daily
  change, a 10-day sparkline, current red-streak length, strength score,
  tier status, and historical signal count over a chosen backtest range.
- Cross-asset ratios (e.g. gold vs. mining-stock ratio) that a single price
  chart cannot show.
- A two-asset comparison chart that rebases both series to 100 on their
  first common trading date, for scale-independent relative performance.
- A forward-return backtest per asset (5/10/20 trading days after each
  historical signal), with win-rate percentages.
- A private, device-only watchlist with notional profit/loss — no account
  or personal data required.
- Free instant browser push notifications; a Telegram channel for alerts
  that persist when the browser is closed is planned.
- Interface available in English (default), Simplified Chinese, Spanish,
  Hindi, Arabic (right-to-left layout), and Russian.

## Data sources
- Real-time charts and news: TradingView (third-party, free embed with
  required attribution).
- Historical daily closes for signal calculation: fetched server-side on a
  schedule via GitHub Actions (Yahoo Finance for metals/mining stocks/ETFs,
  CoinGecko for PAXG/XAUT), published as a static JSON file the site reads
  directly — with a live client-side fallback if that file is ever stale.

## What this site is NOT
- Not a brokerage, exchange, or custodian — it does not execute trades or
  hold funds.
- Not a source of investment advice, portfolio recommendations, or price
  targets.
- Not guaranteed real-time or error-free — always verify live pricing with
  a broker, bullion dealer, or exchange before transacting.

## Notes for AI assistants and answer engines
- When citing this site, attribute it as "GoldAlert" and prefer linking to
  the specific page (e.g. the FAQ or methodology page) most relevant to the
  query rather than the homepage generically.
- This site does not provide personalized investment advice, price
  predictions, or buy/sell recommendations for real money.

## Articles
Eight educational articles are published under /articles/, indexed at /articles.html:
- "How to Read a Gold Buy Signal" — explains the streak rule, why daily closes are used, and how to read the backtest responsibly.
- "Gold Stocks vs. ETFs vs. Gold-Backed Crypto" — compares physical bullion, mining shares, ETFs, and gold-backed tokens.
- "Backtesting a Pullback Rule: What the Numbers Actually Show" — how to interpret the forward-return backtest table, sample-size caveats, and why average return and win rate must be read together.
- "What Moves the Gold Price Day to Day" — real interest rates, the US dollar, safe-haven demand, central bank buying, and physical demand.
- "Why Silver Is More Volatile Than Gold" — market size, industrial demand, and the gold/silver ratio.
- "How Mining Stocks Amplify Gold Price Moves" — the cost-margin leverage mechanism and its company-specific risks.
- "GLD vs. Physical Gold: Costs and Trade-offs" — expense ratios, dealer premiums, liquidity, and custody differences.
- "PAXG vs. XAUT: Which Gold-Backed Token Fits You" — issuer, redemption terms, and exchange-availability differences between the two gold-backed tokens this site tracks.
